result.summary:
### Summary of Changes

1. **Capture Flow** ([`src/ui/screens/capture.ts`](file:///C:/Users/nolan/talking-face/src/ui/screens/capture.ts)):
   - Updated sequence to run `CORE_POSES` (6 poses: Relax, Mmm, Just a bit, Ahh, Eee, Ooo) using all titles and instructions directly from `POSE_PROMPTS`.
   - Single-screen state progression reusing the `MediaStream` continuously across pose captures instead of re-requesting `getUserMedia` on every step. Handled camera rejection with a friendly message and a retry affordance, and ensured full release on unmount and navigation.
   - Added compact progress dots alongside the run-relative counter (`3 / 6` during core, `X / Y` during extended).
   - Displayed a low-pressure decision point after the 6th core pose allowing the user to either finish immediately with a ready-to-use avatar or continue capturing the 5 `EXTENDED_POSES`.
   - Retained all quality checks, friendly rejection guidance, and individual pose retakes.

2. **Preview Screen** ([`src/ui/screens/preview.ts`](file:///C:/Users/nolan/talking-face/src/ui/screens/preview.ts)):
   - Adapted to bake and cycle through whatever partial set of poses was captured without assuming poses other than `REST` exist.
   - Connected the Adjust panel to the currently previewed pose, populated with friendly titles from `POSE_PROMPTS`.
   - Preserved `REST` alignment across incremental bake/merge workflows.

3. **Incremental Upgrade Path** ([`src/ui/screens/settings.ts`](file:///C:/Users/nolan/talking-face/src/ui/screens/settings.ts)):
   - Used [`AvatarStore.getPoseAvailability()`](file:///C:/Users/nolan/talking-face/src/store/avatarStore.ts#L169-L176) to detect missing extended poses.
   - Surfaced an "Improve lip sync" action in Settings whenever poses are missing, launching [`CaptureScreen`](file:///C:/Users/nolan/talking-face/src/ui/screens/capture.ts) specifically for the uncaptured set using the existing neutral `REST` photo without requiring re-capturing or disturbing the base registration.
   - Hidden when all poses are captured.

4. **Frame Inspector** ([`src/ui/screens/inspector.ts`](file:///C:/Users/nolan/talking-face/src/ui/screens/inspector.ts)):
   - Updated to show all 11 poses in canonical order across Grid, Flip, and Difference views.
   - Absent poses are safely handled without empty tiles or crashes and labelled as `(absent)` / "Not captured" so uncaptured poses are distinguishable from captured ones.

5. **Debug Overlay** ([`src/ui/debugOverlay.ts`](file:///C:/Users/nolan/talking-face/src/ui/debugOverlay.ts)):
   - Added the `tongue` control to the articulation readout bar list alongside `jawOpen`, `lipWidth`, `lipRound`, and `lipClosure`.
   - Added an `availablePoses` readout displaying the poses present in the active avatar.
   - Updated timeline colors and pose types to match the 11-pose vocabulary.

6. **Styles** ([`src/ui/screens/screens.css`](file:///C:/Users/nolan/talking-face/src/ui/screens/screens.css)):
   - Added layout and visual styles for progress dots, decision cards, and absent inspector items while preserving all touch targets (`--tap`), responsiveness, and non-scrolling constraints on mobile portrait screens.

---

### Validation

- `npm run typecheck`: **Passed** (0 errors)
- `npm test`: **Passed** (5 test files, 38 tests passed)

order.notes:
This app makes a user's photographed face appear to speak. The pose vocabulary grew from five to eleven. Note OPEN was RENAMED to BIG_OPEN and SMALL_OPEN is a genuinely new pose.

`npm run typecheck` currently fails only in the four UI files this task owns (capture.ts, preview.ts, inspector.ts, debugOverlay.ts). Those errors are the work list. Everything else in the project already compiles and its tests pass; do not touch it.

The governing idea: poses are OPTIONAL. src/core/poses.ts splits them into CORE_POSES (six, required for a working avatar) and EXTENDED_POSES (five, opt-in). Avatar.frames is a Partial record with only REST guaranteed. An avatar with just the core set is fully valid and must play correctly -- the renderer already falls back through the articulation distance metric, so a missing pose needs no special handling in UI.

This matters for the user experience, which is the point of the split: eleven mandatory photographs is a long way to walk before a first-time user (often a child) sees anything work at all, and the extended poses are also the hardest to photograph well. Six gets them a talking face; the rest is an upgrade they choose.

All user-facing copy comes from POSE_PROMPTS in src/core/poses.ts. Never invent pose copy, and never let a pose id, phonetic term or the words viseme/phoneme/landmark reach the screen.
